Where Is the Model Looking?

Your job: find out whether a heatmap can be trusted. First, look at where model B's evidence comes from and cover parts of the patch to test it. Then put two models with almost the same accuracy side by side and decide which one you would deploy.

The model
VGG19, blocks 4–5 fine-tuned on CBIS-DDSM mass vs. no-mass patches Test AUC Sensitivity Specificity Calls "mass" when score ≥
Station 1 · about 6 min

Nine test patches, model B

0most evidence
Cover a square (click the patch)
Click anywhere on the patch to hide that square from the model.
Covered scores are simulated from how much of the model's Grad-CAM evidence (for both classes) the square hides. A real occlusion test reruns the network.
Layer
Explain which class
ReLU at the end
Nothing positive for this class at this layer: every weighted sum was negative, so ReLU leaves an all-zero map.
αk = mean over pixels of ∂ymass / ∂Ak
ReLU( Σk αk · Ak )  with A from block5

yc is the score for the class you picked. Ak is the k-th feature map of the chosen layer. αk says how much nudging that map would raise the score, which is the same gradient backprop uses to train.

The heatmap is a weighted sum

The six block5 maps with the largest α for the predicted class, each scaled to its own range. Grad-CAM adds all 512 of them, weighted by α, and keeps the positive part.

Station 2 · about 5 min

Same task, two models

Model A was our first try. Model B was retrained after we changed how the no-mass patches were cut. Their test AUCs differ by 0.004. Pick a mass and compare where each one looks. Click either patch to cover the same square for both.

Pointing hit rate: share of the 94 test masses where the hottest Grad-CAM pixel (block5, class "mass") falls inside the radiologist's outline.

Try this

  1. Station 1. On a true positive, cover the hottest spot with a large square. How far does the score fall? Now cover a dark spot of the same size.
  2. Open the false positive. Where is the model looking? Cover that spot: does the call flip to "no mass"?
  3. On a true positive, switch from block5 to block3. Why is the block3 map sharper? Use the map sizes under the layer buttons.
  4. Turn the ReLU off, then ask for the "no mass" explanation. What do the newly visible regions stand for?
  5. Station 2. On Mass 1, where does model A look? Cover the mass for both models. Which score barely moves, and what is model A really using?
  6. The two AUCs are almost the same. Which model would you deploy, and which number on the cards told you?

Debrief: "Grad-CAM shows where the evidence came from. Does that prove the model is right?" After the workshop, a short Slido quiz asks what you saw at each station.

Patches: Sawyer-Lee R, Gimenez F, Hoogi A, Rubin D. Curated Breast Imaging Subset of DDSM (CBIS-DDSM). The Cancer Imaging Archive, 2016. doi:10.7937/K9/TCIA.2016.7O02S9CY. CC BY 3.0. Grad-CAM: Selvaraju RR et al. "Grad-CAM: Visual Explanations from Deep Networks via Gradient-based Localization." ICCV 2017.
